title: Diner-Style Home Fries
summary: Diced potatoes are parboiled until just tender, then fried in butter and oil with browned onion and paprika for a crisp, golden diner-style breakfast side.
equipment: large heavy frying pan (30 cm), cast iron if possible

ingredients.item: all-purpose or waxy potatoes (such as Yukon Gold), scrubbed and cut into 1.5 cm cubes
fine sea salt or table salt, for the water
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Brown the onion
steps.text: Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in the frying pan over medium-high and cook the chopped onion for 8-10 minutes, stirring now and then, until deeply browned. Tip it into a bowl and set aside; browning it separately builds a sweet, caramelised flavour without it turning mushy once mixed back in later.

steps.title: Parboil the potatoes
steps.text: Cover the potato cubes with 1 cm of cold water in a saucepan, add the salt and bring just to the boil, about 6 minutes. Drain immediately and let them steam-dry for 2 minutes in the colander. This brief par-cook softens the inside of the potato so it's tender by the time the outside turns crisp in the pan.

steps.title: Fry in a single layer
steps.text: Heat the remaining oil and the butter in the pan over medium-high until the butter is foaming. Add the potatoes in a single layer so each piece touches the hot pan, then leave them undisturbed for 4-5 minutes until browned underneath. Resisting the urge to stir lets a solid crust form before the pieces are turned.

steps.title: Turn and crisp further
steps.text: Turn the potatoes and repeat the process 2-3 more times, for 12-15 minutes in total, until crisp and golden on every side. A thin metal spatula makes it easier to get underneath the crust without tearing it.

steps.title: Finish with onion and spice
steps.text: Stir the browned onion, paprika, salt and pepper into the pan and cook for 1 minute to warm through and let the spice bloom in the hot fat. Scatter over the chopped parsley just before serving for a fresh finish.

tips: Cut the potato cubes to an even 1.5 cm so they parboil and fry at the same rate.
A common mistake is skipping the steam-dry step - wet potatoes release moisture into the pan and steam instead of crisping.
Use a well-seasoned cast iron or heavy non-stick pan; a thin pan loses heat too fast for a good crust to form.
Don't stir too often while frying - leaving the potatoes undisturbed for each 4-5 minute stretch is what builds the crust.
storage: Keep in the fridge for up to 2 days in an airtight container; they don't freeze well, as the texture turns soft on thawing. Reheat in a hot pan until piping hot (74°C) rather than in the microwave, to bring back some crispness. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
